clue.text: Clear description of nose in Lear

definitions.meaning: clear in the sense of shining, giving out light
Edward Lear's nonsense poem The Dong with a ... Nose gives its hero a glowing nose

explanation.surface: A request for a plain account of how Edward Lear pictured a nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer of nonsense verse; the Dong's nose shines in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing with light is bright and plain to see, hence clear; Lear applies the same adjective to the Dong's nose.

clue.text: Not expecting girl to have the goods

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
wares are goods for sale

explanation.surface: A surprised girl takes possession of merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken unawares is to be caught by surprise, off guard.

clue.text: Rising prices catch Frenchmen -a sore point

indicators.note: catch means the rising prices hold the Frenchmen inside them

parts.note: inflation is a general rise in prices
MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, French gentlemen

explanation.surface: Price rises hit French people, which is a sensitive topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sore point' looks figurative, a touchy subject; read literally it is a red, painful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation is swelling and redness on the body, literally a painful patch.

clue.text: Son not fancying a day's sport?

definitions.meaning: a son is a shoot off the family tree, a descendant
read as two words, not up for a day out shooting game

explanation.surface: A son who does not feel like a day out shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a descendant or side branch of a family; split in two it suggests skipping a shooting party.

clue.text: No person mixed up letters so much

definitions.text: No person mixed up letters so much

parts.words: No person mixed up letters so much
parts.note: the Oxford don famous for accidentally swapping the opening sounds of words

explanation.definitionFit: William Archibald Spooner gave his name to the slips where initial sounds trade places, so no one jumbled letters more.

clue.text: Diplomats' turn to relax

parts.note: the United Nations is the body of diplomats
a bend is a turn in a road

explanation.surface: Diplomats take their turn to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbend is to loosen up and become less formal or stiff.

clue.text: She ranks higher in England than in France

definitions.text: She ranks higher in England than in France

parts.words: She ranks higher in England than in France
parts.note: in Britain this is a title of honour for women; across the Channel the same word simply means lady

explanation.definitionFit: The British honour for women matches a knighthood, while the French word of the same spelling just means a woman.

clue.text: Ximenes was so important

definitions.meaning: Francisco Jimenez de Cisneros, Ximenes, was a Spanish prince of the church in red
a ... point or number is fundamental, of chief importance

explanation.surface: A remark on how significant Ximenes was.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximenes was also the pen name of a famous Observer crossword setter, which makes 'important' tempting; the first sense is the Spanish churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Ximenes was a senior Catholic prelate, and cardinal also means of chief importance.

clue.text: Prospect for gold in American state

indicators.note: the gold sits inside the name of the Central American country

parts.note: Panama is a state, a nation, in Central America
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Prospecting for gold somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect for gold' looks like the verb PAN, but 'Prospect' alone is the noun for a view, and 'state' means a country, not a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of scenery, the same as a sweeping vista.

clue.text: The Israelites worshipped such golden skin

definitions.meaning: in Exodus the Israelites made and worshipped a golden idol of a young cow
the leather from a young bovine is a fine skin for bookbinding and shoes

explanation.surface: A remark on what the Israelites worshipped and on gold-coloured hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exodus idol was a young bovine in gold, and the hide of such a young animal is a prized leather skin.

clue.text: Act irresponsibly, causing boss to resign?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for panicking or behaving rashly
a firm whose chief walks out is left without its leader, read literally

explanation.surface: Reckless behaviour that forces the boss out of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to panic and behave rashly; taken literally, an organisation whose chief quits is left without its top person.

clue.text: House Territorial divisions in the South-Eastern area

parts.note: a home is a house
counties are territorial divisions of a country

explanation.surface: Houses and county boundaries in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, such as Surrey and Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The counties encircling London form the prosperous region of south-east England.

clue.text: Game where you can rhyme 'credit' with 'pulpit'

parts.note: CR is the accountant's abbreviation for credit
an ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early churches

explanation.surface: A parlour game in which an odd pair of words is supposed to rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like examples of rhyming; really they are the wordplay, 'with' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is an old parlour game in which one player gives a word and the others must find rhymes for it.

clue.text: Poem by Donne? You can hear why I'm confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the poet's name and the sounded words are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the phrase why I'm is taken as it sounds, the letter Y followed by I'M

parts.note: said aloud this is Y plus I'M

explanation.surface: Was this poem by John Donne? Hear me explain my confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne did not write it: Keats did. 'You can hear' turns 'why I'm' into Y, I, M, and 'confused' mixes those with DONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endymion is the long poem by John Keats about the shepherd loved by the moon goddess.

clue.text: Sort of pea? Sort of grass, rather

indicators.note: rather marks a correction, so the words before are recast into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrects themselves: not a kind of pea, more a kind of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sort of' looks like the anagram signal, but SORT itself is fodder with PEA; 'rather' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish and North African grass used for making paper and rope.

clue.text: It's criminal to make lover die horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters suffer a ghastly scrambling

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making a lover die in a gruesome way is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer who commits wicked acts is a criminal.

clue.text: Policeman knocks back drinks on the rocks

indicators.note: knocks back, as of a drink, here means the whole assembly is turned around
a drink on the rocks is served with ice in it, so the ice goes inside the drinks

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat does
rocks is slang for ice in a drink

explanation.surface: A policeman downs drinks served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks back' reads as swallowing; it reverses LAICEPS, ICE inside LAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A special constable is a volunteer British police officer, commonly called a special.

clue.text: Top strategist may be floored by this

definitions.meaning: split in two, the word suggests a monarch of schemes, the best of planners
boards laid down to make a floor

explanation.surface: A master tactician might be knocked flat by this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floored' looks like defeated; it means given a floor of boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is boards used for flooring, and split it suggests a supreme schemer.

clue.text: Enough of our time is taken, having to correspond

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era
to equate is to correspond or match

explanation.surface: Enough of our time is being used up by having to write letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspond' suggests writing letters; it means to match, as in equate.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient, just enough for the need.

clue.text: Shoe that pinches?

definitions.meaning: one who steals furtively, pinch being slang for steal

explanation.surface: A shoe that is too tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneaker is a soft sports shoe, and also someone who sneaks off with things, pinching them.

clue.text: Trader has morning in club for exercise

indicators.note: the morning abbreviation goes inside the name of the club

parts.note: an Indian club is a bottle-shaped club swung in gymnastic exercise
AM, ante meridiem, means morning

explanation.surface: A businessman spends the morning at his gym club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a social club; it is an Indian club, the weighted wooden bottle swung for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Indiaman was a large merchant sailing ship trading with India, a trading vessel.

clue.text: Concerning the sea-battle in which I was taken prisoner

indicators.note: taken prisoner means the I is held inside the name of the battle

parts.note: the Marne was the site of First World War battles in France

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a naval battle in which they were captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-battle' reads as one idea; the hyphen hides the split after 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine means relating to or found in the sea.

clue.text: Sharpness of a two-thirds cut applied to workforce

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word means its first two letters

parts.note: the men are the workers of a firm

explanation.surface: A two-thirds pay cut imposed on the staff, done with a keen edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keenness of judgment, mental sharpness or shrewdness.

clue.text: Main meal a potato skin? You'll need this dressing!

parts.note: dinner is the main meal of the day
a jacket is the skin of a baked potato, as in jacket potato

explanation.surface: A dinner of baked potato that will need a salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests a sauce for the potato; it means getting dressed for a formal evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The black tuxedo jacket is formal evening wear, so dressing for a smart dinner calls for one.

clue.text: Dandy heard to grind his teeth.

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken for their sound

parts.note: to gnash is to grind the teeth

explanation.surface: A fop who is heard grinding his teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was the famous 18th-century dandy and master of ceremonies at Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard 'Beau' Nash was a celebrated Georgian fashion leader, the archetypal dandy.

clue.text: Terrorists' handmaiden?

definitions.meaning: belonging to the Irish Republican Army, a terrorist group
in Antony and Cleopatra one of the queen's two maids bears this name

explanation.surface: Asking who serves as maid to a terrorist group.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Cleopatra has two attendants, Charmian and Iras.
explanation.definitionFit: IRA's is the possessive of the Irish republican paramilitaries, and Iras is a servant of Cleopatra in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Hide safely in French fort

parts.note: en is French for in
a sconce is a small fort or earthwork

explanation.surface: Taking cover in a French fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce is to settle or tuck something away in a secure place.

clue.text: Come home to Bognor terrace

definitions.meaning: an idea that comes home to you sinks in, is taken in
playfully, a terrace in the seaside town of Bognor Regis

explanation.surface: Returning to a row of houses in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is an English seaside resort; a row of its houses becomes, whimsically, a Regis terrace, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact sinks in it is noted by the mind, as an entry is recorded in a book of records.
